instructions: Take the 1 lb steak out of the fridge about 20 minutes before you cook it, and pat it dry.

Meanwhile, make the dressing. Finely chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro stems. Pound them with the garlic clove and a pinch of the salt in a mortar until you have a smooth paste. No mortar? Mince them together, then press the side of your knife over them on the board until they turn to paste.
Juice the 3 limes to get 6 tbsp. Scrape the paste into a jar or bowl and add the lime juice, 1/4 cup fish sauce, 1 1/2 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp of the oil. Shake or stir until the sugar dissolves.
Taste the dressing. It should taste sour first, then salty, then a little sweet. If it's flat, add a splash more fish sauce.

Halve the cherry tomatoes. Very thinly slice half the red onion. Halve the cucumber lengthwise and slice it into half moons. Pick 1/2 cup cilantro leaves and 1/2 cup mint leaves, plus a few extra of each for the top. Finely chop the 1/2 cup peanuts.
Thinly slice 2 chilies into a small bowl for the table.
Heat a heavy skillet over high until it's smoking. Rub the steak with the last 1 tbsp oil and sprinkle it all over with the rest of the salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper.

Lay the steak in the pan and leave it alone for 2 minutes, until the underside is deep brown. Flip it and cook the other side for 2 minutes. That's medium rare for a steak about 3/4 inch thick. You're cooking it to 125°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Press the middle: it should feel soft with a little spring, like the base of your thumb.
Move the steak to a plate, cover it loosely with foil and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Put the salad greens in a wide bowl and toss them with 1 tbsp of the dressing. Pile them onto a platter.
Slice the steak thinly across the grain. Put it in the bowl with the tomatoes, onion, cucumber, cilantro and mint, pour over most of the remaining dressing and toss gently.
Pile the beef and vegetables over the greens. Scatter over the peanuts and extra leaves and drizzle with the last of the dressing.
Serve right away, with the sliced chilies on the side.
method_notes: All three read versions sear or grill the steak, rest it, slice it thin against the grain and toss it in a lime juice, fish sauce and sugar dressing with tomato, red onion, cucumber and cilantro, mint or green onion. RecipeTin Eats pounds chilli, garlic and cilantro stems into a paste for the dressing, sears sirloin in a smoking hot pan for 2 minutes a side, and finishes with peanuts over dressed lettuce. Foodiecrush marinates rib eye in ponzu, sesame oil and ginger first and serves lettuce on the side; Hungry in Thailand adds sesame oil and carrot. This one follows RecipeTin Eats for 4 and moves the chilli out of the dressing to the side.
